# New renderings — odyssey-109 (22.292–397)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| βοῶν ἑλίκων ἐπιβουκόλος (22.292) | "the herdsman of the crumple-horned cattle" | "the herdsman of the cattle with crumpled horns" | "the cowherd" alone (reserved for βουκόλος), "twisted-horned", "curved-horned"; follows the shipped βοῶν ἐπιβουκόλος ἀνήρ and the table’s ἕλικας βοῦς |
| Δαμαστορίδης (alone, 22.293; patronymic standing for Agelaus) | "Damastor’s son" | "the son of Damastor" | "Agelaus" (the name is not in the Greek; the note gives it); follows the table’s Ἀτρεΐδης alone "the son of Atreus" |
| αὐτοσχεδόν (22.293) | "at close quarters" | "at close quarters" | "hand to hand", "point-blank", "from near" |
| ἔγχος μακρόν (22.293, ἔγχεϊ μακρῷ) | "a long spear" | "his long spear" | "tall", "great spear"; ἔγχος is "spear" as in the table’s ἄλκιμον ἔγχος |
| μέσον κενεῶνα (22.295; κενεών the soft hollow of the side below the ribs) | "in the middle of the flank" | "in the middle of the flank" | "belly", "groin", "waist", "loins" |
| διαπρὸ δὲ χαλκὸν ἔλασσεν (22.295) | "and right through the bronze he drove" | "and drove the bronze clean through" | "pierced", "thrust through", "sent the bronze"; ἐλαύνω is "drive" here and "strike" at ἤλασε (22.296) |
| πρηνής (22.296) | "face down" | "on his face" | "headlong" (that is ἐρείπω’s own sense), "prone", "forward" |
| φθισίμβροτος αἰγίς (22.297, φθισίμβροτον αἰγίδ’) | "the mortal-destroying aegis" | "her mortal-destroying aegis" (+ note: the aegis is not described here; φθίω is 'perish, waste', here causative) | "man-slaying", "death-dealing", "life-wasting", "terrible aegis"; βροτός is "mortal", as in φαεσίμβροτος "the Sun, who gives light to mortals" and τερψίμβροτος "the mortal-delighting Sun"; "aegis" is a transliteration kept as the table’s αἰγίοχος "aegis-bearing" does |
| ἐπτοίηθεν (22.298, of the suitors’ wits) | "were terrified" | "were thrown into a panic" | "fluttered", "were scattered", "fled" (that is ἐφέβοντο); φρένες is "wits", as in φρένες ἐσθλαί |
| αἰόλος οἶστρος (22.300; αἰόλος also 'gleaming, dappled') | "the darting gadfly" | "a darting gadfly" (+ note: αἰόλος also 'gleaming, dappled') | "gleaming", "dappled", "shifting" (each picks one sense silently); οἶστρος is the "gadfly" (not "wasp", "horsefly") |
| ἐδόνησεν (22.300, gnomic aorist of δονέω) | "drove wild" | "drives them wild" | "shook", "tormented", "maddened", "stung" |
| αἰγυπιοὶ γαμψώνυχες ἀγκυλοχεῖλαι (22.302) | "vultures, crook-taloned, hook-beaked" | "hook-taloned, hook-beaked vultures" | "eagles" (αἰετός), "sea-eagles" (that is φήνη), "curve-beaked"; follows the shipped "crook-taloned" / "hook-taloned" for γαμψώνυχες (odyssey-079) and the table’s αἰετὸς ἀγκυλοχείλης "hook-beaked"; the note says the species is not known |
| ἐπιστροφάδην (22.308; adverb in -δην from ἐπιστρέφω) | "turning from one to another" | "wheeling from one man to the next" | "in every direction", "indiscriminately", "without pause", "headlong" |
| στόνος ἀεικής (22.308) | "a groaning, unseemly" | "an unseemly groaning" | "hideous", "ugly", "shameful" (ἀεικής is "unseemly" as in ἀεικέα πότμον and ἔργον ἀεικές) |
| καί μιν λισσόμενος ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (whole line, 22.311 = 22.343 = 22.366) | "and him, entreating, winged words he spoke:" | "and, entreating him, spoke winged words:" | "beseeching", "begging", "supplicating"; "addressed" (reserved for προσέφη); follows the shipped "entreating" for λισσόμενος (odyssey-034) and the table’s ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα |
| γουνοῦμαί σ’, Ὀδυσεῦ· σὺ δέ μ’ αἴδεο καί μ’ ἐλέησον (whole line, 22.312 = 22.344, opening a plea) | "I beseech you at your knees, Odysseus; and you, revere me, and pity me;" | "I entreat you, Odysseus; and you, show me respect and take pity on me;" | "have mercy", "spare me", "fear the gods"; follows the table’s γουνοῦμαί σε, ἄνασσα (6.149), and "revere" / "show respect" for αἰδέομαι as in αἰδέσσομαι (14.388); "pity" as in ἐλέησεν |
| οὐ γάρ πώ τινά φημι ... εἰπεῖν οὐδέ τι ῥέξαι ἀτάσθαλον (22.313–314) | "For never yet, I say, to any of the women in the halls have I said or done any wanton thing;" | "For I tell you that I have never yet said or done anything wanton to any of the women in the halls;" | "reckless", "outrageous"; ἀτάσθαλον is "wanton" as in the table’s ἀτάσθαλα "wanton deeds" and ἀτάσθαλος "wanton" |
| παύεσκον (22.315, iterative of παύω) | "I used to stop" | "I used to stop" | "I would stop" in `l` (hides the -σκ- suffix), "I restrained" |
| τηλοῦ ἐμοὶ νόστοιο τέλος γλυκεροῖο γενέσθαι (22.323) | "far from me the fulfilment of sweet homecoming to be" | "that the fulfilment of a sweet homecoming should be far from me" | "the end of my homecoming" (τέλος is "fulfilment" as in τέλος θαλεροῖο γάμοιο), "pleasant", "dear" (γλυκερός is "sweet") |
| δυσηλεγής (22.325, θάνατον δυσηλεγέα; sense uncertain) | "painful" | "painful" (+ note: from δυσ- and the root of ἄλγος, but ἀλέγω 'heed', 'pitiless', is another guess; the sense is not certain) | "grievous" (reserved for λυγρός / ἀλεγεινός), "bitter" (πικρός), "pitiless" (νηλεής), "hateful" (στυγερός), "grim" |
| ἀποπροέηκε (22.327, of a sword) | "had dropped" | "had let fall" | "had thrown away", "had let go" |
| φθεγγομένου ... κάρη κονίῃσιν ἐμίχθη (22.329) | "as he was speaking, his head in the dust was mingled" | "as he was speaking, his head was mingled with the dust" | "rolled in the dust", "fell", "was thrown"; ἐμίχθη is "was mingled" |
| Τερπιάδης (22.330) | "Terpes’ son" | "son of Terpes" | "Terpiades" (transliterated patronymic); follows the table’s Εὐηνορίδης "son of Evenor" |
| ἀλύσκω (22.330 ἀλύσκανε, 22.363 and 22.382 ἀλύσκων, with κῆρα μέλαιναν) | "shunning" (ἀλύσκανε: "was shunning") | "keeping clear of" (ἀλύσκανε: "was trying to keep clear of") | "escaping", "fleeing", "avoiding" (ἀλύξαι and ἀλύξας are "escape" in the shipped odyssey-025 and odyssey-052); follows the shipped "shunning" for ἀλυσκάζων (odyssey-087) |
| ἑρκείου (of Zeus, 22.334–335, Διὸς μεγάλου ... ἑρκείου) | "of great Zeus, of the courtyard" | "great Zeus of the courtyard" (+ note: ἑρκεῖος from ἕρκος 'enclosure', the god of the house’s enclosure) | "Zeus Herkeios" (a transliteration), "guardian of the home", "of the fence" (the table keeps "fence" for ἕρκος ὀδόντων) |
| αὐτοδίδακτος (22.347) | "self-taught" | "self-taught" | "taught by himself", "untaught" |
| ἐνέφυσεν (22.348, οἴμας ... ἐνέφυσεν) | "implanted" | "has implanted" | "breathed into", "made grow", "put" |
| παραείδειν (22.348; rare compound, sense taken from the parts) | "to sing beside" | "to sing before (you)" (+ note: exact sense not certain) | "to sing for", "to sing with", "to accompany" |
| δειροτομῆσαι (22.349) | "to cut-the-throat" | "to cut my throat" | "to behead", "to slaughter", "to kill" |
| τὸν δ’ ἐπιμειδήσας προσέφη πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς (whole line, 22.371) | "Him then smiling at addressed many-wiled Odysseus:" | "Then Odysseus of many wiles, smiling at him, spoke to him:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "said to him with a smile"; same frame as the table’s τὸν δ’ ἄρ’ ὑπόδρα ἰδὼν προσέφη πολύμητις Ὀδυσσεύς |
| κακοεργίη · εὐεργεσίη (22.374) | "evil-doing" · "well-doing" | "doing evil" · "doing good" | "wickedness", "kindness", "benefaction"; εὐεργεσίη keeps the εὖ- of the table’s εὐεργός "who does well" |
| πολύφημος (of Phemius, 22.376; sense uncertain) | "many-voiced" | "many-voiced" (+ note: 'of many voices', for a singer, or 'much spoken of'; the choice is not certain) | "famous", "much-sung", "renowned" (each picks one sense silently); not to be confused with the name Polyphemus |
| πάντοσε παπταίνοντε, φόνον ποτιδεγμένω αἰεί (whole line, 22.380, said of two men) | "glancing everywhere, slaughter expecting always" | "glancing about on every side, always expecting slaughter" | "waiting for death", "looking for the killing"; φόνος is "slaughter" as at 22.375 ἐκ φόνου |
| ὑποκλοπέομαι (22.382, εἴ τις ... ζωὸς ὑποκλοπέοιτο; rare verb) | "was hiding away" | "was ... hiding" (+ note: rare verb, sense from κλέπτω 'steal' and the context) | "skulking", "lurking", "stealing away" |
| δίκτυον πολυωπόν (22.386) | "a net, many-meshed" | "a many-meshed net" (+ note: πολυωπός is rare; the sense, 'with many openings', comes from ὀπή; 'many-eyed' is the other possibility) | "many-eyed", "close-woven", "wide-meshed" |
| κέχυνται · κέχυντο (of fish and of suitors, 22.387, 22.389) | "lie poured out" · "lay poured out" | "lies scattered" · "lay scattered" | "were heaped", "sprawled", "lay strewn"; χέω is "pour" and the word keeps the image in `l` |
| τό μοι καταθύμιόν ἐστιν (22.392) | "which to me is in-the-heart" | "the word I have on my mind" | "that I desire", "pleasing to me" (the word is built on κατά + θυμός, and the note says so) |
| κινήσας δὲ θύρην (22.394) | "having moved the door" | "he pushed at the door" (+ note: the Greek does not say whether he pushed it open or rattled it) | "knocked", "opened the door", "shook the door" (each picks one reading) |
| παλαιγενής (voc. παλαιγενές, 22.395) | "of ancient birth" | "of great age" | "old-born", "ancient", "long-lived"; the table’s παλαιή "aged" is the plain adjective |
| σκοπός (of Eurycleia over the maids, 22.396) | "watcher" | "overseer" | "lookout" (kept for the 22.156 sentry-sense of the same word), "guardian", "keeper"; `l` keeps the table’s "watcher" |
| ἔρχεο· κικλήσκει σε πατὴρ ἐμός, ὄφρα τι εἴπῃ (whole line, 22.397) | "Come; he calls you, my father, so that he may say something." | "Come: my father is calling you, so that he may tell you something." | "go" (ἔρχεο is "go" in the table where it sends someone away; here the speaker beckons), "summons", "wants you" |
